stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under core NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of Meta's Llama family indicates continued high relevance in the large language model space.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
stories.author: Zhonglei He
bullet_points: Introduces NemotronLabs VoiceChat, an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model.
Features native tool-calling capabilities, allowing the model to reason and invoke external functions.
Utilizes a unified streaming architecture combining encoders, decoder-only LLMs, and specialized output streams for real-time interaction.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The mention of Llama-3 indicates ongoing industry interest in Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for persistent AI agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and 8VC.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local large language models.

stories.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
stories.author: Andy Greenberg, WIRED.com
bullet_points: Google's threat intelligence team successfully infiltrated a major supply-chain hacking group, TeamPCP.
The operation involved placing an undercover analyst within the criminal organization's inner circle.
This highlights the ongoing, high-stakes battle between major tech firms and sophisticated cybercriminal syndicates.

stories.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
stories.author: Fuli Luo
bullet_points: Introduces CodeMidas, a new agentic pipeline designed to scale Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments for coding agents.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods by using entire source codebases as a rich source of diverse, executable RL tasks.
Transforms implemented functionality within existing code into verifiable RL environments, moving beyond reliance on simple artifacts like commits or issues.

stories.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
stories.author: Hiskias Dingeto
bullet_points: Proposes a novel 'Lie Detector Test' for Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect concealed knowledge.
Addresses the ambiguity where an LLM might intentionally withhold knowledge or genuinely lack it, which is undetectable via standard output.
Adapts the forensic Concealed Information Test (CIT) to measure a stronger response when an LLM is presented with true vs. decoy information.

stories.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
stories.author: Zhonglei He
bullet_points: Introduction of NemotronLabs VoiceChat, an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model.
The model features native tool-calling capabilities, allowing it to reason and invoke external functions.
Its architecture integrates streaming components for simultaneous listening, transcription, reasoning, and speech generation.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Bungie says it’s ‘not done with Destiny’ and will bring back vaulted content
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Bungie is reversing its Destiny Content Vault policy to restore previously vaulted content.
The restored content includes older campaigns, destinations, and raids in Destiny 2.
This decision addresses player backlash following the controversial removal of paid legacy content.

stories.title: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is settling a $250 million class-action lawsuit regarding unfulfilled AI upgrades to Siri.
The settlement specifically targets owners of iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, and iPhone 16 models purchased after June 10, 2024, in the US.
Eligible iPhone owners can now submit claims to receive a payout from the settlement.

stories.title: I got to see Google’s wild ideas about the future of laptops
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: Google is showcasing future concepts for its 'Googlebook' laptop.
The device features polished hardware and a familiar Chromebook-like OS.
A key feature is the deep integration between the laptop and the user's Android phone, making them feel like a single unit.

stories.title: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio tears through our benchmark tests
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio features a powerful configuration: 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 256GB RAM, and 4TB storage.
The device is positioned as a high-end machine specifically targeting demanding AI workloads, rather than general content creation.
The top-tier configuration carries a significant price tag of $12,299.

stories.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
stories.author: Asim Kadav
bullet_points: Introduces 'Designer-RSI,' a framework for agentic graphic design, treating it as a long-horizon task.
Utilizes a frozen frontier model to operate professional design software via over 230 tools.
Features an external procedural memory that accumulates and refines reusable design procedures from user experience.

stories.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw
stories.author: Lingyao Li
bullet_points: The research investigates how users prioritize values when delegating tasks to autonomous AI agents, moving beyond simple task completion metrics.
The study analyzed 73,093 Reddit posts regarding the OpenClaw agent, categorizing user feedback across human values and agent aspects.
It identifies six key value groups (e.g., Autonomous, Dependable, Equitable Access) that users prioritize in their AI interactions.

stories.title: Gricea: An Open Science Platform for Conversational AI Research
stories.author: Ziang Xiao
bullet_points: Gricea is an open-science platform designed to standardize and share conversational AI (CAI) research.
The platform addresses fragmentation in CAI studies by representing research as configurable, deployable artifacts.
Its goal is to enable researchers to easily run, inspect, share, and reuse existing CAI studies for better knowledge accumulation.

stories.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Jie Yang
bullet_points: Introduces DiaVLo, a new diagnostic framework for Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
Addresses the critical need to verify that VLMs exhibit desired and avoid harmful behaviors for reliable deployment.
Leverages human curation and VLM generation capabilities to build specifications of VLM behaviors.

stories.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
stories.author: Hossein Rahnama
bullet_points: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents (BCA) to model opinion dynamics in LLM agents.
BCA separates an agent's internal beliefs (probabilities) from its external speech.
Uses a single prior-strength parameter ($\kappa$) to control agent stubbornness and persuasion receptivity.

stories.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence
stories.author: Leela Krishna
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical decision-making process for robots experiencing task failure.
It proposes a framework for robots to decide whether to self-diagnose, use other sensors, or request human intervention.
A controlled simulation benchmark is built to test these decisions based on the diagnostic power and reliability of sensor data.

stories.title: BrainWideBench: Benchmarking large-scale pretraining and across-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings
stories.author: Eva L. Dyer
bullet_points: Introduces BrainWideBench, a new benchmark for evaluating large-scale neural data.
Aims to test the potential of general-purpose neural representations learned across diverse animals and brain regions.
Addresses limitations in current research caused by fragmented evaluation protocols and narrow task focus.

stories.title: Predictable Failure in Multi-Hop Retrieval: Score-Distributional Confidence Scoring and Abstention
stories.author: Andre Bacellar
bullet_points: The paper identifies that failures in multi-hop retrieval are not random but cluster in structurally predictable query subpopulations.
It proves that confident-failure reduction is possible if retrieval features share mutual information about success, a condition met by LLM-judge pipelines.
This work helps explain the performance gap (AUC-AC) observed between LLM-based and dense-only retrieval systems.

stories.title: Particle Competition and Cooperation for Robust Graph Convolutional Network Learning Under Label Noise
stories.author: Fabricio Breve
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of label noise sensitivity in Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs).
It introduces PCC+GCN, a novel hybrid framework that integrates Particle Competition and Cooperation (PCC).
PCC functions as a pre-training label-refinement stage to identify and correct suspicious node labels before GCN training.

stories.title: Available Guardrails: Certifying Selective Prediction across ML Systems
stories.author: Michael Chaykowsky
bullet_points: The paper addresses the need for 'selective predictors' in ML systems, which act as safety gates to ensure predictions meet a required level of trustworthiness.
A core challenge identified is the difficulty of generating a formal 'certificate' of reliability using only finite calibration data, especially as safety requirements become stricter.
This research is highly relevant to deploying reliable AI in critical domains (e.g., policy labeling, patient subgroups) where certified accuracy is mandatory.

stories.title: $λ$-Controlled GRPO: Turning Flow-Matching Ratio Instability into a Budgeted Resource
stories.author: Ramit Pahwa
bullet_points: The research addresses instability in training flow-matching models when using reinforcement learning (RL) for alignment.
It introduces $\lambda$-Controlled GRPO to manage the systematic policy update changes across multi-step denoising.
The core technical contribution is reframing the flow-matching ratio instability as a budgeted resource problem.

stories.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention
stories.author: Richard Zhe Wang
bullet_points: The paper proposes that adding 'abstention' and 'noise filtering' primitives to softmax attention improves language model pretraining.
Abstention allows an attention head to output nothing, circumventing the standard requirement that attention weights must sum to one.
Noise filtering enables the value pathway of an attention head to selectively suppress unwanted information.

stories.title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency
stories.author: Chunlei Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in LLM memory systems: the lack of a mechanism to decide whether retrieved memories should be trusted.
Standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) fails when memory stores contain conflicting information, leading to amplified hallucinations.
Proposes an 'Interpretable Memory Decision Controller' using three-signal complementarity to decouple confidence and consistency in memory usage.

stories.title: QuranicMMLU: A Cognitively-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Generative AI Solutions on Quranic Linguistic Knowledge
stories.author: Ehsaneddin Asgari
bullet_points: Introduces QuranicMMLU, a new benchmark designed to evaluate generative AI specifically on Quranic Arabic.
Moves beyond simple Q&A by structuring evaluation across five linguistic pillars: Phonology, Morphology, Syntax, Semantics, and Pragmatics.
Addresses a gap in existing benchmarks by stratifying evaluation based on linguistic complexity and cognitive demand.

stories.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Jie Yang
bullet_points: Introduces DiaVLo, a new diagnostic framework for Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
Addresses the critical need to verify that VLMs exhibit desired and non-harmful behaviors for reliable deployment.
Leverages human curation and VLM generation capabilities to construct specifications of observed and desired behaviors.

stories.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention
stories.author: Richard Zhe Wang
bullet_points: The paper proposes that adding 'abstention' and 'noise filtering' primitives to softmax attention improves language model pretraining.
Abstention allows an attention head to output nothing, circumventing the standard constraint that attention weights must sum to one.
Noise filtering enables the value pathway of an attention head to selectively suppress irrelevant information.

stories.title: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
stories.author: Bowen Zhou
bullet_points: Introduces RecreationWorld, a framework for hybrid Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) that combine graphical interaction and code-based software development.
The core concept is 'recreation': agents must autonomously discover and replicate a given running reference environment.
This addresses the real-world need for CUAs to seamlessly interleave interface exploration with software implementation and verification.

stories.title: Moral Entropy: Auditing Bias and Uncertainty in Moral Judgment
stories.author: Maciej Skorski
bullet_points: Proposes 'Moral Entropy,' a Bayesian framework to model and learn from annotator disagreement in moral judgment tasks.
Challenges the conventional practice in computational ethics of treating annotator disagreement as noise to be discarded.
Decomposes uncertainty into aleatoric uncertainty, representing irreducible disagreement about the moral content.

stories.title: Show HN: Foremerge – Catch Intent Conflicts Between Parallel Coding Agents
stories.author: foremerge
bullet_points: The tool, Foremerge, addresses a critical problem in parallel AI coding agent workflows.
It aims to catch logical intent conflicts (e.g., conflicting architectural changes) before they become integration nightmares.
This is relevant for teams using multiple autonomous coding agents on a single codebase.

stories.title: Architecting a Resilient DevSecOps Pipeline for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Presents a four-stage DevSecOps CI/CD architecture specifically designed for securing enterprise AI agents.
Integrates several key security tools, including GitHub Actions, secret scanning, Veracode SCA, and Pipeline SAST.
Highlights the use of AI-assisted review within the pipeline for enhanced security posture.

stories.title: How to stop AI from confidently shipping broken code (a pattern that actually works)
stories.author: infoinlet1
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world problem: AI generating seemingly correct but functionally broken code.
Focuses on practical solutions or patterns to mitigate the risk of AI-introduced bugs.
Relevant to software development, AI tooling, and code quality assurance.

stories.title: Building Bivack: A Cloud Dev Sandbox for Coding Agents on AWS Lambda MicroVMs
stories.author: gunnargrosch
bullet_points: Introduces 'Bivack,' a cloud development sandbox designed for running coding agents.
Leverages AWS Lambda MicroVMs to provide isolated, per-user execution environments.
Offers accessibility via a browser terminal or VS Code workbench with persistent storage on S3.
